# qompack micro-benchmark baseline — recorded by SP-01, the first checkpoint (V1).
#
# Recorded with the command V1-VERIFY §7 P-13 uses for comparison, but at -count 10 rather than
# -count 5: benchstat needs at least 6 samples to report a confidence interval, so a 5-sample
# baseline can only ever be compared point-to-point.
#
#     go test -run '^$' -bench . -benchmem -count 10 -p 1 ./...
#
# Host: Windows 11, Intel Core Ultra 7 155H, NTFS. This host has high per-syscall filesystem
# latency — an isolated fsync measures ~2.1 ms and a create+write+close ~0.65 ms. The two
# I/O-bound entries below are dominated by that, and will look very different on the Linux CI
# runners. Treat a large improvement there as a change of machine, not a change of code; the
# allocation columns are the platform-independent half of this file.
#
# Budgets from SP-01's Definition of Done item 16, and how this recording compares:
#
#     BenchmarkHistogram_Observe        < 100 ns/op    MET      19.09n ±13%
#     BenchmarkConfigLoad_ColdNoFiles   < 2 ms/op      MET      950.5µ ± 6%
#     BenchmarkHookNoop_InProcess       < 3 ms/op      MISSED   5.322m ± 4%
#     BenchmarkPathsWriteAtomic_4KB     < 2 ms/op      MISSED   4.718m ± 8%
#
# Both misses are filesystem-bound on this host rather than algorithmic, and both are recorded
# honestly rather than restated to fit:
#
#   - PathsWriteAtomic_4KB cannot reach 2 ms here by construction. §4.6 requires an fsync of the
#     staged file before the rename, and a bare fsync alone costs ~2.1 ms on this machine — more
#     than the whole budget, before WriteAtomic does any work of its own.
#
#   - HookNoop_InProcess spends its time on syscalls the wave-0 hook repeats on every single
#     invocation: EnsureLayout's directory creation, a fresh logger open, and the observation
#     append. Allocations are flat at 2300/op across every sample, so this is I/O, not garbage.
#     SP-05's resident daemon is what removes it — caching the layout and the logger is precisely
#     the work budget B-A (hook p99 < 15 ms) assumes has already been done. This number is the
#     headroom measurement the benchmark exists to provide, and it says the no-op path currently
#     consumes about a third of B-A before SP-08 observes anything at all.
#
goos: windows
goarch: amd64
pkg: github.com/qompack/qompack/internal/cli
cpu: Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 7 155H

# --- SP-07 (internal/dag), appended by the dependence-DAG subplan ---

#     go test -run '^$' -bench . -benchmem -benchtime 20x -count 10 -p 1 ./internal/dag/

# letting Go calibrate b.N against a 1s target would spend minutes on those two alone for no extra

# as the same flags are used on both sides.

# SP-06 — content-addressed store, redaction, exact token accounting (V2).
#
# Recorded with the same command shape as the SP-01 block above, but at -count 6
# rather than -count 10 (benchstat's minimum for a confidence interval) and
# restricted to the benchmarks that complete in seconds:
#
#     go test -run '^$' -bench <subset> -benchmem -count 6 -p 1 ./internal/store ./internal/redact ./internal/tokens
#
# Host: Windows 11, Intel Core Ultra 7 155H, NTFS — the same machine as the
# SP-01 block, and the same caveat applies with more force. SP-06's budgets are
# specified against the CI LINUX RUNNER. A CPU profile of the store's misses
# attributes 90.9% of the time to runtime.cgocall (i.e. raw syscall cost, with
# zstd decode at 1.4%), and open() is roughly 10x cheaper on Linux, so the
# I/O-bound rows below are platform measurements rather than algorithmic ones.
# RE-MEASURE ON LINUX BEFORE TREATING ANY OF THEM AS A REAL MISS.
#
# These numbers are also load-sensitive to an unusual degree. An earlier run of
# the same benchmarks on a busy machine reported every figure 3-4x worse
# (Redact_100KB_NoSecrets at 2.6 ms rather than 0.61 ms). The block below was
# taken on a quiet machine; a wildly different reading is a statement about the
# host, not the code.
#
# Measured medians against the subplan's budget table:
#
#     BenchmarkEstimateRoot_64Cached              <= 5 us      MET      2.2 us
#     BenchmarkUnits_100KB                        <= 500 us    MET      163 us
#     BenchmarkOpenSpan_4KB_of_4MB                <= 150 us    MET      91 us
#     BenchmarkMarkEncoded_100                    <= 1 ms      MET      519 us
#     BenchmarkRedact_100KB_NoSecrets             <= 2 ms      MET      607 us
#     BenchmarkGetChunk                           <= 60 us     MISSED   304 us
#     BenchmarkRedact_100KB_NoSecretsButKeyword   <= 2 ms      MISSED   10.21 ms
#     BenchmarkRedact_100KB_WithSecrets           <= 2 ms      MISSED   37.50 ms
#
# The two redaction misses are NOT platform effects and must not be read as
# such. Each of the ten built-in rules costs >= 2 ms for a single RE2 pass over
# 100 KB on its own, so the 2 ms budget is unreachable for any payload that
# requires even one full scan. The mandatory-literal prefilter is what makes the
# dominant no-secret case 0.6 ms instead of 32 ms, but it can only buy speed by
# SKIPPING, so it buys nothing once a rule genuinely has to run. Collapsing the
# ten rules into one alternation was measured and is 0.53-0.67x — slower, since
# the merged NFA costs more per byte than the passes it saves. See the SP-06
# subplan's spec-resolutions table (D19) and V2-VERIFY §2.6a ②.
#
# NOT RECORDED HERE, because each takes minutes on this host and would dominate
# the run. Figures measured separately during implementation, same machine:
#
#     BenchmarkPutBytes_100KB_Cold      <= 3 ms     22.9 ms  (syscall-bound)
#     BenchmarkPutBytes_100KB_Warm      <= 400 us   227 us with an inert
#                                                   redactor; ~1 ms as shipped
#     BenchmarkOpenStore_50kRoots       <= 400 ms   404 ms
#     BenchmarkSearch_1000Roots         <= 25 ms    69.5 ms (text query; a
#                                                   path/tool/symbol query is
#                                                   0.44 ms)
#     BenchmarkGC_50kObjects            <= 2 s      2.42 s
#
# Note BenchmarkGC_50kObjects previously seeded only 4,000 objects while naming
# 50k; it now genuinely builds ~50k, so its figure is not comparable to anything
# recorded before SP-06.
################################################################################

#
# ============================================================================================
#
# internal/sketch — recorded by SP-03, the sketch library (V2).
#
# RE-RECORDED IN FULL after the whole-branch review's fix round. The MinHash sampler was replaced
# (bottom-k over distinct shingle hashes; see ADR 0030 §9a), so its two rows had to move — and
# because six other rows moved by 10.8–23.6 % at p < 0.05 between the two recordings, this block is
# ONE fresh run rather than two rows spliced into the old samples. Those six — BloomTest, CMSAdd,
# CMSEstimate, HLLAdd and HLLCardinality down, MisraGriesAdd up — are hashing paths this round did
# not touch, and the earlier recording carried ±8–25 % intervals against this one's ±1–13 %, so what
# moved is the machine's noise floor rather than the code. Mixing runs to avoid re-recording has
# already cost this branch one review finding; the whole block is replaced instead.
#
# Recorded at -count 10 rather than the subplan's -count 6, for the reason the header above
# already gives: benchstat needs at least 6 samples to report a confidence interval, and this
# host is noisy enough that 6 samples cannot separate a budget from a busy minute. That is not
# an assumption. A -count 6 pass over an identical binary reported BenchmarkBloomAdd at
# 491.5n ±256% and BenchmarkBloomTest at 1.417µ ±111% — three to seven times the -count 10
# medians, from the same code, minutes apart. Every verdict here is a benchstat median over ten
# samples; none is a single run, and every sample below comes from ONE recording.
#
#     go test ./internal/sketch -bench=. -benchmem -count 10 -run '^$'
#
# Host: Windows 11, Intel Core Ultra 7 155H. Unlike the V1 block above, nothing in this package
# touches the filesystem, so none of these numbers are syscall-bound — they are CPU and cache,
# and they should look better on the Linux CI runners rather than different in kind. The
# allocation columns are again the platform-independent half of the recording.
#
# Coverage at this commit, measured with `go test ./internal/sketch/... -cover`:
# internal/sketch 96.5%, internal/sketch/sketchtest 99.5%, against the 90% floor
# (00-ARCHITECTURE §6.4). The sketch figure MOVES by a couple of tenths between runs and nothing
# has regressed when it does: property_test.go draws fresh values from rapid on every run, so
# which defensive branches get exercised differs run to run.
#
# Budgets from the SP-03 implementation spec's performance table (00-ARCHITECTURE §13
# invariant 9), and how this recording compares.
#
# Latency:
#
#     BenchmarkBloomAdd            ≤ 1.0 µs/op        MET      157.9n ± 3%   6.3× headroom
#     BenchmarkBloomTest           ≤ 1.0 µs/op        MET      161.9n ± 3%   6.2×
#     BenchmarkCMSAdd              ≤ 1.0 µs/op        MET      159.7n ± 1%   6.3×
#     BenchmarkCMSEstimate         ≤ 1.0 µs/op        MET      160.8n ±13%   6.2×
#     BenchmarkHLLAdd              ≤ 1.0 µs/op        MET      132.2n ± 5%   7.6×
#     BenchmarkHLLCardinality      ≤ 25 µs/op         MET      6.819µ ± 7%   3.7×
#     BenchmarkMisraGriesAdd       ≤ 5 µs/op amort.   MET      103.8n ± 6%    48×
#     BenchmarkL0SketchUpdate      ≤ 5 µs/op          MET      494.3n ±11%  10.1×
#     BenchmarkMinHash4KiB         ≤ 1.5 ms/op        MET      287.1µ ± 7%   5.2×
#     BenchmarkMinHash100KiB       ≤ 2.5 ms/op        MET      1.381m ± 5%   1.8×
#     BenchmarkBloomMarshal        ≤ 60 µs/op         MET      6.111µ ±27%   9.8×
#     BenchmarkBloomUnmarshal      ≤ 60 µs/op         MET      4.539µ ± 6%  13.2×
#     BenchmarkCMSMarshal          ≤ 250 µs/op        MET      37.70µ ±23%   6.6×
#     BenchmarkCMSUnmarshal        ≤ 250 µs/op        MET      32.80µ ±30%   7.6×
#     BenchmarkRebuildBloom5000    ≤ 15 ms/op         MET      931.2µ ±12%  16.1×
#
# Allocation — six rows carry an allocation budget, and all six meet it:
#
#     BenchmarkBloomAdd            0 allocs/op        MET      0 allocs/op, 0 B
#     BenchmarkBloomTest           0 allocs/op        MET      0 allocs/op, 0 B
#     BenchmarkCMSAdd              0 allocs/op        MET      0 allocs/op, 0 B
#     BenchmarkCMSEstimate         0 allocs/op        MET      0 allocs/op, 0 B
#     BenchmarkHLLAdd              0 allocs/op        MET      0 allocs/op, 0 B
#     BenchmarkL0SketchUpdate      0 allocs/op        MET      0 allocs/op, 0 B
#
# Those six rows did NOT start out zero, and the provenance is the most useful thing in this
# block. Read this before treating a future non-zero reading as a new defect:
#
#   The first recording of these benchmarks — the run that added them — measured every hashing
#   row at exactly 1 alloc/op and 32 B/op, the composite at 3 and 96 B, and
#   BenchmarkRebuildBloom5000 at 5 004 allocs/op and 172 400 B/op. Every latency budget was met
#   throughout, which is the point: a nanosecond column cannot show an allocation, and nothing
#   in the tree had measured one until these benchmarks existed. The plan's rationale column
#   for those rows reads "one SHA-256 of a short key plus 7 bit tests" and did not anticipate
#   that the shared helper allocated.
#
#   The cause was one line in core.HashBytes, not anything in internal/sketch: it ended
#   `copy(out[:], h.Sum(nil))`, and h.Sum(nil) allocates the 32-byte digest slice it appends
#   into. The two rows that hash nothing — HLLCardinality and MisraGriesAdd — were already flat
#   at 0, which is what localised it. HashBytes now writes the digest into the returned array
#   with `h.Sum(out[:0])`. A ONE-OFF A/B probe of the two forms (8 samples, not among the
#   samples below) put them at 1 alloc/op / 104.1n ±2% and 0 alloc/op / 90.36n ±3% with
#   byte-identical digests. TestHashBytes_DoesNotAllocate in internal/core/hash_test.go is the
#   durable guard, placed where the function lives.
#
#     BenchmarkL0SketchUpdate      3 allocs, 96 B      → 0 allocs, 0 B
#     BenchmarkRebuildBloom5000    5 004 allocs        → 4 allocs
#                                  172 400 B           → 12 400 B  (exactly 5 000 × 32 B saved)
#
#   Those allocation deltas are exact and platform-independent. The LATENCY deltas across these
#   recordings are not attributable to the fix: there have now been four full recordings on this
#   host — pre-fix, post-fix, post-review and this one — and each ran under different machine
#   load, while three of them also changed fixtures. Do not quote a percentage from row-to-row
#   differences as a property of any one change; the allocation columns are the only half of the
#   comparison that is clean.
#
# BenchmarkL0SketchUpdate's Bloom probe is a HIT, and that is a deliberate fixture choice:
#
#   sketches/tried.bloom holds negative-knowledge DESCRIPTORS (§8.3), never paths, so the
#   composite gets its own filter pre-filled with the descriptors it probes. The first two
#   recordings probed a filter built from path keys, which every descriptor missed by
#   construction — not the production filter at all, and undisclosed at the call site.
#
#   In production most probes DO miss, since most descriptors have never been eliminated, and a
#   miss returns at the first clear bit instead of reading all seven positions. This row
#   therefore reports the less common case on purpose, because a budget-model input should be
#   the conservative number. What the choice is worth was measured, in a one-off probe run
#   (count=12, both variants side by side, not among the samples below): the composite is
#   498.0n ±7% with a hit against 486.5n ±3% with a miss, and Bloom.Test alone 174.7n ±5%
#   against 166.2n ±5%. The short-circuit is worth ~8–12 ns, about 2% of the composite, because
#   Test is dominated by the one SHA-256 in hash128 rather than by the seven probes it guards.
#
# The two MinHash rows are the ones this recording exists for, and both IMPROVED:
#
#     BenchmarkMinHash4KiB     367.5µ ± 6%  →  287.1µ ± 7%   (-21.9%, p=0.000, n=10)
#     BenchmarkMinHash100KiB   1.525m ± 5%  →  1.381m ± 5%   ( -9.4%, p=0.000, n=10)
#
#   That direction is not obvious and is worth explaining, because the change ADDED work: the
#   sampler now selects the 8 192 smallest DISTINCT shingle hashes (an open-addressed set, a
#   quickselect refinement) where it used to keep everything below a rate-derived threshold. Two
#   restructurings paid for it and then some. Shingle hashing moved into a batch helper whose
#   default-width loop has a compile-time-constant shingle length, so the compiler unrolls FNV-1a's
#   multiply chain and overlaps consecutive shingles — 323 µs against 580 µs for the 102 393
#   shingles of a 100 KiB document, measured in isolation. And hashing and permuting are now two
#   passes over a batch rather than one interleaved loop, which is worth a further ~90 µs at 4 KiB.
#   The selection machinery itself costs ~0.25 ms at 100 KiB; the two restructurings return ~0.4 ms.
#
#   The straightforward implementations of the same rule do NOT fit: admit-everything-and-narrow
#   measured 2.87 ms against the 2.5 ms budget, and sort-and-truncate 8.2 ms. Those figures come
#   from a standalone A/B harness, not from this run, and are recorded because "we chose the fast
#   one" is worth nothing without the numbers that made the others unusable.
#
#   BenchmarkMinHash100KiB's ALLOCATION moved and the row does not carry an allocation budget:
#   3 072 B / 2 allocs → 396 288 B / 4 allocs. The selector's two structures are the whole of it —
#   a 32 768-slot table (256 KiB) and a 16 384-value buffer (128 KiB) — and they are sized from
#   MinHashSampleTarget rather than from the document, so a 1 MiB input allocates exactly the same
#   396 KiB as a 100 KiB one. BenchmarkMinHash4KiB is unchanged at 3 072 B / 2 allocs: at or under
#   the target no selection runs and the batch buffer stays on the stack.
#
#   The 100 KiB row was the tightest in this file and still is, now at 1.8× headroom rather than
#   1.6×. The history is worth keeping: the FIRST recording of it, under a loaded run, had a median
#   of 2.432m against the 2.5 ms budget with four of ten samples ABOVE budget and a ±43% interval,
#   and was recorded MARGINAL. A quieter machine, not a code change, is what moved it then. Re-
#   deriving these numbers on CI hardware is a V2-VERIFY task, and this row must be judged with
#   benchstat over repeated samples, never one run.
#
#   It is also the row that least deserves alarm. MinHash is deliberately NOT on the hook path: it
#   runs in the daemon's async worker under budget B-C (l0_process, p99 < 50 ms, soft), which it
#   clears by more than 35×. The 2.5 ms figure is a cost bound on the sampler, not a latency
#   guarantee to a caller.
#
# BenchmarkMisraGriesAdd's budget says "amortized" and the word is load-bearing. The k = 256
# table is full only at the moment of a decrement pass: every counter holds 1, so one pass wipes
# all 256, the next 256 Adds refill it down the has-room fast path, and about one iteration in
# 257 pays the two O(k) map passes. That cycle is the algorithm's steady state under a
# unit-weight stream, not a fixture artefact, and it is what the Misra-Gries potential bound
# predicts. One decrement pass in isolation measured 7.9µ in a one-off probe — 1.6× the whole
# row, and again not among the samples below. bench_test.go's benchSaturatedMG documents why a
# fixture that suspends the bound measures a cost the code cannot be driven into.
#
# The composite line is what this subplan owes the L0 model. BenchmarkL0SketchUpdate is the
# whole of §8.1 item 5's contribution to a PostToolUse — one CMS.Add, one HLL.Add, one
# Bloom.Test — and at 494.3n ±11% with zero allocations it is 0.003% of the 15 ms B-A hook
# budget, against the 0.03% the plan allowed for. Both halves of that budget are met.
#
goos: windows
goarch: amd64
pkg: github.com/qompack/qompack/internal/sketch
cpu: Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 7 155H

# --- SP-05 additions (V2, task 7 — hot-path bench harness, three-platform bench gate) -----------
#
# Recorded with the same command as above:
#
#     go test -run '^$' -bench . -benchmem -count 10 -p 1 ./...
#
# on the same Windows 11 / Intel Core Ultra 7 155H / NTFS host. Each is tied to a named budget
# (task-7-spec.md's "Benchmarks tied to a named budget" table):
#
#     BenchmarkReadState         < 100 us/op (hot-path prelude)      MET   ~52-60 us/op
#     BenchmarkEncodeRequest     < 5 us/op (4 KB payload)            MET   ~1.1-1.5 us/op
#     BenchmarkIngestAccept      B-B (l0_ingest, p99 < 2ms)          MET   ~3.3-3.7 us/op
#     BenchmarkServerRoundTrip   daemon-side B-A portion, p99 < 2ms  MET   ~42-63 us/op
#
# BenchmarkReadState is filesystem-bound (one os.ReadFile of a 32-byte record) rather than
# algorithmic, same caveat this file's own header gives BenchmarkPathsWriteAtomic_4KB above: this
# host's per-syscall latency is high, and Linux CI runners will likely report a lower number. It
# is still comfortably under its own 100us budget here.
#
# BenchmarkServerRoundTrip drives a real listener (named pipe on this host) end to end per
# iteration — connect, write, ACK, close — so it is the closest in-repo proxy for B-A's own
# daemon-side portion (excluding process spawn, which only a real-process harness can measure; see
# test/bench/hotpath and task-7-report.md for that measurement).
goos: windows
goarch: amd64
pkg: github.com/qompack/qompack/internal/ipc
cpu: Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 7 155H
